summary: Defines a protocol that carries SS7 MTP2 user signaling messages over IP using SCTP. It runs between a Signaling Gateway, which receives SS7 signaling from the telephone network, and a Media Gateway Controller.

eli5.summary: The old phone network has its own language for setting up calls. This document lets those messages travel across the internet so old and new systems can still talk.

questions: how is ss7 carried over ip with sctp
how does m2ua fail over between servers
subtitle: How a phone-network signalling link is extended over IP so a remote controller can run the upper layers of SS7.

tldr.problem: Telephone networks signal with SS7. A gateway at the edge of the IP network terminates the SS7 link, but the software that handles call processing may sit somewhere else.
tldr.mechanism: M2UA lets a Signalling Gateway terminate SS7 up to MTP Level 2 and carry the MTP Level 3 messages over SCTP to a Media Gateway Controller, which keeps the MTP2 to MTP3 boundary working as if the link were local.
tldr.outcome: A Standards Track protocol that defines the message formats, ASP and AS state handling, fail-over modes and link management for this backhaul.

facts.label: Default timers
facts.value: T(r) 2 s, T(ack) 2 s, T(beat) 30 s

sections.title: Backhauling SS7 Over IP
sections.content:
RFC 3331 defines M2UA, the SS7 MTP2 User Adaptation Layer. It carries the messages of the user of SS7 Message Transfer Part Level 2 (that user is MTP Level 3) over IP using the Stream Control Transmission Protocol (SCTP, RFC 2960). The word backhaul means moving signalling from the point where it arrives back to the point where calls are processed.

Two parties are involved. The Signalling Gateway (SG) sits at the edge of the IP network, receives SS7 over a standard SS7 interface and acts as a Signalling Link Terminal. The Media Gateway Controller (MGC) is the other end. The SG terminates SS7 up to MTP Level 2, and the MGC terminates MTP Level 3 and above.

M2UA fits the framework in RFC 2719, which pairs a common signalling transport with an adaptation module for each kind of signalling. M2UA is the adaptation module for MTP2 users.
sections.eli5: One computer plugs into the old phone wires, and another computer far away decides what to do with the calls. M2UA is how the first passes everything it hears to the second.

sections.title: Gateways, Servers and Interface Identifiers
sections.content:
The RFC defines a small vocabulary. An Application Server (AS) is a logical entity serving one application, for example an MGC handling MTP Level 3 for SS7 links that the gateways terminate. An Application Server Process (ASP) is one process instance of an AS, such as an active or standby MGC. At the gateway, an AS is modelled as an ordered list of one or more ASPs.

Each SS7 link is identified by an Interface Identifier. The M2UA layer MUST keep a map from the identifier to a physical interface on the gateway (such as a V.35 line or a T1 or E1 line or time slot), and from the identifier to an SCTP association and stream. Values are of local significance only, agreed between the SG and the ASP. The integer format MUST be supported; the text format MAY be.

Redundancy follows an n+k model, where n ASPs are the minimum needed and k are available to take over. The RFC notes that 1+1 active/standby and a simplex 1+0 setup are subsets of it.
sections.eli5: Every phone wire gets a nickname. The gateway keeps a list of which nickname goes to which wire and which far-away computer, and it can switch to a spare computer if one breaks.

sections.title: Message Format
sections.content:
Every M2UA message starts with a common header of Version (value 1 means release 1.0), a spare byte, Message Class, Message Type and a 32-bit Message Length. After the header come zero or more parameters in tag-length-value form, with mandatory parameters before optional ones. Everything is in network byte order.

Each parameter has a 16-bit tag and a 16-bit length. The total length MUST be a multiple of 4 bytes, with zero padding of at most 3 bytes that is not counted in the length field. Common tags fall in the range 0x00 to 0xff, and M2UA-specific tags in 0x300 to 0x3ff. For the user-data messages (class 6) an Interface Identifier parameter follows the common header; its integer form uses tag 0x1 and length 8, and its text form uses tag 0x3 with a string of at most 255 octets.

The message classes M2UA uses are Management (0), ASP State Maintenance (3), ASP Traffic Maintenance (4), MTP2 User Adaptation (6) and Interface Identifier Management (10).
sections.eli5: Each message has a short label on the front saying what kind it is and how long it is. The contents are packed in boxes that are always a whole number of four-byte units, with empty filler if needed.

sections.title: Link Messages and Boundary Procedures
sections.content:
MTP2 User Adaptation messages carry the MTP2 to MTP3 interface across IP. Data carries one MTP2-user PDU starting at the Signalling Information Octet, with an optional Correlation Id that lets a newly active ASP synchronize and be acknowledged by a Data Acknowledge message. The MGC controls the state of the link: an Establish Request asks to bring the link in service, and a Release Request takes it out of service.

State Request performs actions such as setting or clearing local processor outage, emergency alignment, flushing buffers or auditing the link, and the gateway answers with a State Confirm that reflects the value. State Indication reports events such as the remote entering or leaving processor outage. Congestion Indication reports congestion and discard levels, sent only when a level actually changes. Retrieval messages support the MTP3 changeover procedure by fetching the BSN and queued PDUs.
sections.eli5: The faraway computer can tell the gateway to switch a phone line on or off, pause it, or report how clogged it is, and the gateway answers back and shouts if something happens on its own.

sections.title: ASP and AS States and Traffic Modes
sections.content:
The gateway tracks the state of every remote ASP. An ASP is ASP-DOWN initially, becomes ASP-INACTIVE after the ASP sends ASP Up and is acknowledged, and becomes ASP-ACTIVE after ASP Active. An SCTP communication-down or restart indication sends it back to ASP-DOWN.

The AS has four states: AS-DOWN, AS-INACTIVE, AS-ACTIVE and AS-PENDING. AS-PENDING is entered when the last active ASP leaves the active state. A recovery timer T(r) starts and incoming messages are queued. If an ASP becomes active before it expires, the queue is delivered; if not, the queue is discarded.

An ASP Active message can carry a Traffic Mode Type. In Override mode the new ASP takes over all traffic, and the previously active ASP is told with a Notify. In Load-share mode the ASPs share traffic. In Broadcast mode every active ASP receives all traffic. Only one mode can be used within an AS.
sections.eli5: A spare computer starts asleep, then wakes up, then takes over the work. If the working one drops out, the gateway holds incoming messages for a couple of seconds, hoping a replacement shows up.

sections.title: Link Key Management and Timers
sections.content:
Optional Interface Identifier Management lets an ASP register dynamically. In a Registration Request it supplies a Link Key (a signalling data link and terminal pair). The gateway can authorize it against existing entries, create a new entry if it supports dynamic configuration, or answer with an error such as Invalid Link Key, Overlapping (Non-Unique) Link Key, Permission Denied, Link Key not Provisioned or Insufficient Resources. De-registration removes an ASP from an AS without necessarily deleting the Link Key data.

Recommended timer defaults are T(r) 2 seconds, T(ack) 2 seconds and T(beat), the heartbeat timer, 30 seconds. The RFC also recommends using SCTP streams for performance. Stream 0 SHOULD NOT carry MTP2 user adaptation messages because it should be used only for ASP management messages.
sections.eli5: A helper computer can ask to be put in charge of a particular phone line, and the gateway either agrees or gives a reason why not.

sections.title: Security and IANA Considerations
sections.content:
M2UA carries telephony signalling, so it has to serve the end users, the network providers and the applications. The stated objectives are availability, integrity and confidentiality of user data transport. SCTP supplies protections against blind denial of service attacks, flooding, masquerade and improper monopolization of services.

Where more than one party operates the network and security cannot be assumed, the RFC recommends IPsec for confidentiality of the payload. If IP addresses and ports must also be masked, it says IPsec ESP SHOULD be used, with ISAKMP for key management.

For IANA, the SCTP Payload Protocol Identifier for M2UA is 2. New message classes, types and parameters are assigned by IETF Consensus.
sections.eli5: Because these messages run real phone calls, the RFC says to lock the traffic in a secure tunnel if you cannot trust everyone on the network.
